video_caption: The video opens with a black screen displaying white text, stating: "This video is purely for educational purposes and must not be used for commercial purposes. Acknowledgment: Christian Medical Association of India, Lady Hardinge Medical College New Delhi, Kakatiya Medical College Warangal, Hindlabs New Delhi, GYD Lab Hyderabad." (The text describes the educational nature and licensing of the video, disclaims commercial use, clarifies attribution, and acknowledges contributing institutions). This screen fades to a dark blue background with a grey header that reads "Haemoglobin by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" and below it "Learning Objectives". White text bullet points appear below, stating: "The objective of this video is to apprise the viewer about the estimation of haemoglobin by Drabkin's method. The video highlights: Principle, Procedure, Quality control, Result interpretation." This screen then transitions to a solid dark blue background before displaying the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" in yellow text at the center. Below this, a yellow arrow pointing right appears, followed by the blue text "Internationally recommended method for determining hemoglobin".

The video segment features a dark blue background with a subtle, textured pattern. At the top, the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" is displayed in golden text, followed by the subtitle "Principle" in a light blue hue. At the 0:04 mark, the text "Blood + Reagent solution (Potassium cyanide and potassium ferricyanide)" appears in light green. An arrow then animates onto the screen, pointing downwards, followed by the appearance of the text "Converts Hb to methemoglobin" in the same light green color at 0:09, explaining the next step in the principle. Another downward-pointing arrow animates onto the screen, and at 0:14, the text "Cyanmethemoglobin" appears, indicating the final converted product. The last part of the segment, at 0:17, shows the beginning of a new line of text, "Absorbance is measured in", starting to appear at the bottom before the segment ends, implying the subsequent step in the measurement process.

The video segment opens with a dark blue background displaying the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" at the top. Below this, a main heading "Principle" is shown. Several bullet points appear sequentially, outlining the principle: "Blood + Reagent solution (Potassium cyanide and potassium ferricyanide)", followed by arrows indicating steps: "Converts Hb to methemoglobin", then "Cyanmethemoglobin", and finally "Absorbance is measured in". Underneath this, two sub-bullet points appear: first, "> Spectrophotometer at a wavelength of 540nm", and then "> Colorimeter using a yellow green filter". The scene then transitions to a new main heading "Equipment". An image of two micropipettes (one grey, one white) appears on a white background, accompanied by the text "> Micropipette". This is replaced by an image of a beige colorimeter/spectrophotometer device, with the text "> Colorimeter or Spectrophotometer". Two sub-bullet points then appear below this, stating "Principle applied - Same" and "Wavelengths available for estimation - Differ", explaining that while the principle is the same for both devices, the available wavelengths for estimation differ.

The video segment details the reagents required for Hb estimation by the Cyanmethemoglobin Method, specifically focusing on Drabkin's solution. The initial screen (0:05-0:11) displays a white bottle labeled "Drabkin's solution" and text indicating "Reagents required," "pH of the solution-7.0-7.4," and "Unstable if exposed to light." This transitions (0:11-0:18) to an image of a brown borosilicate bottle, also labeled "Drabkin Solution," with added text stating it should be "Stored at room temperature in brown borosilicate bottles for several months." Following this (0:18-0:23), a test tube containing a clear, pale yellow liquid is shown, accompanied by the text "Solution should be clear and pale yellow in color," visually representing the expected appearance of Drabkin's solution. Finally (0:23-0:33), a person wearing white gloves operates an ELICO CL 223 COLORIMETER. They place a test tube with a pale yellow liquid into the device. The colorimeter's display shows "CAL 54" and then "0.00 54." The person presses the "ST" (standard) and "OD" (optical density) buttons, setting the display to "0.00 54," indicating the blanking of the instrument against what is described as water, at a wavelength of 540 nm, before the audio cuts off.

The video segment displays a presentation slide with a dark blue background. At the top, in a light blue font, is the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" (English). Below this, in a larger, brighter blue font, is "Reagents required" (English). On the left side of the screen, a large white plastic bottle with a red and black label is shown, sitting on a light-colored surface. Below the bottle, the text "Drabkin's solution" (English) is written in white. On the right side, a bullet point states, "Room temperature > 30°C then store in refrigerator but brought to room temperature before use" (English), indicating storage instructions for the Drabkin's solution. No people are visible, and the scene is static throughout the segment.

The video segment features a presentation slide with a dark blue gradient background. At the top, the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" is displayed in white text. Below this, in a teal font, is the subtitle "Reagents required". On the left side of the screen, an image framed by a gold border shows a gloved hand holding a small brown glass bottle with a red screw cap. The label on the bottle is partially visible, showing text like "globin Test", "H.G. Standa", and "10 ml". Below this image, the text "Hb Standard solution" is written in white. On the right side, a list of bullet points appears progressively. The first bullet point states "Available commercially at a specific concentration". The second bullet point reads "Stored in a brown bottle as it is photosensitive". At the 0:08 mark, the third bullet point animates onto the screen, stating "Exposure to light causes deterioration in the strength of the standard". Finally, at the 0:13 mark, the fourth bullet point appears, which says "The concentration of the standard used in this demonstration is 14.8 gm% (Derivation of this number will be discussed later)".

The video segment opens with a title slide displaying "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" at the top and "Reagents required" below. Two images are shown: on the left, a test tube rack holds several clear tubes and one purple-capped tube filled with a dark red liquid, labeled "Venous blood in EDTA tube"; on the right, a gloved hand uses a lancet to prick a finger, labeled "Capillary blood by finger prick," with "Sample" written at the bottom of the screen. The scene then transitions to a dark blue background with the text "Procedure" in the center. Subsequently, a person in a lab coat, wearing gloves, uses a pipette to dispense a clear yellowish liquid (Drabkin's solution) from a white bottle into a test tube placed in a metal rack. A digital timer showing "0:00.00" is visible in the background. The gloved hand then picks up a purple-capped test tube containing a blood sample, gently inverting it to mix. Next, the hand uses a pipette to draw approximately 0.02 milliliters of blood from a small tube (which has blood stains on its exterior). The outer surface of the blood-filled pipette is then carefully wiped with a white tissue to remove any excess blood. Finally, the gloved hand places the pipette into a test tube in the rack, which already contains the yellowish Drabkin's solution, and slowly expels the blood. As the blood mixes with the solution, the liquid in the test tube immediately changes color to a reddish-orange, demonstrating the reaction taking place. The video ends showing the test tube rack with the newly reddish-orange solution alongside the other yellowish tubes.

The video segment opens with a gloved hand inserting a test tube containing an orange-brown liquid into a beige Ellico CL 223 Colorimeter. The colorimeter's digital display, which shows "OUTPUT" and "WAVELENGTH," initially reads "2.00 54" as the test tube is placed, then quickly changes to "0.05 54", and finally settles on "0.32 54" where "54" likely indicates a wavelength of 540 nanometers. The instructions on the device's label mention adjusting optical density to zero using a blank solution. The scene then transitions to a dark blue background with text appearing in the center. The top text reads "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method," indicating the topic of the procedure. Below this, the text "Calculate the hemoglobin concentration" appears, highlighting the next step in the process.

The video segment features a dark blue background with text displaying the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" in white, followed by "Calculate the hemoglobin concentration" in light blue. Below this, a formula is prominently shown: "> Conc. of Hb in sample = (Absorbance of sample / Absorbance of standard) X Conc. of standard." This formula, presented in white and green text, illustrates how to calculate the concentration of hemoglobin (Hb) in a sample by comparing its absorbance to that of a known standard, a common method in spectrophotometry. No people or actions are visible, as the segment consists solely of this static textual information.

The video segment opens with a dark blue background displaying the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" in gold text, followed by "Calculate the hemoglobin concentration" in light blue italicized text. Below, two green bullet points appear, stating: "Concentration of standard is available on the kit insert" and "Measure its absorbance or OD against a blank of Drabkin's solution." The scene then transitions to a new title, "Preparation of Standard curve for Hemoglobin estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin method," also in light blue italicized text, with the main title remaining at the top. The video then shows a laboratory setting where a person wearing white gloves and a gold bracelet points to a large white bottle labeled "Hemoglobin Cyannmethemoglobin Method" and a smaller amber vial labeled "Hemoglobin 2.0 Gm%." In the background, test tube racks hold multiple test tubes, some containing a yellow liquid. The scene returns to the dark blue background with the same titles. A green bullet point states, "The concentration of the standard used in this demonstration is 14.8 gm%" with a grey parenthetical note, "(Derivation of this number will be discussed later)." Finally, another green bullet point appears, "A WHO International reference HiCN standard is also available commercially as 10ml sealed ampoules & is stable for years," followed by "Make serial dilutions of the standard solution with Drabkin's solution" appearing below it.

The video segment opens at 0:05 showing a person wearing white gloves holding a test tube filled with a yellow liquid, which they carefully place into the first slot of a metal test tube rack already containing multiple empty test tubes. In the background, a white device with red buttons, likely a piece of lab equipment, is visible. Concurrently, a light blue table on the right displays the title "Preparation of Standard curve for Hemoglobin estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin method." The table has columns labeled "TT No." (Test Tube Number), "Std Vol (mL)" (Standard Volume in milliliters), "Drabkin's solution Vol (mL)" (Drabkin's solution Volume in milliliters), and "Dilution factor." The first row of the table, corresponding to "TT No." 1, shows "0" under "Std Vol (mL)", "5" under "Drabkin's solution Vol (mL)", and "0 (0/5)" under "Dilution factor." The overarching title at the top of the screen is "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" (Hemoglobin Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method). As the segment approaches 0:10, the person begins to prepare another test tube, which appears to contain a reddish-brown liquid, for placement in the next slot of the rack.

The video segment details the preparation of a standard curve for hemoglobin estimation using the Cyanmethemoglobin method. It begins with a slide displaying a table for preparing the standard curve, along with the "Strength of the standard = 14.8 gm/dL" and the formula "Value of Hb = Dilution factor X Strength of the standard". The table initially shows the "TT No.", "Std Vol (mL)", "Drabkin's solution Vol (mL)", and "Dilution factor" columns filled, and then progressively populates the "Value of Hb" column with calculated values (0.0, 2.9, 5.9, 8.9, 11.8, 14.8). The scene then transitions to a laboratory setting where a person wearing white gloves is shown. This person is seen holding a test tube containing a yellow solution and placing it into an ELICO CL 223 COLORIMETER. The colorimeter's display changes from "CAL 54" to "0.00 54", indicating that the instrument is being blanked at a wavelength of 540 nm using Drabkin's solution. After blanking, the person prepares to measure diluted samples. The video then switches back to the table slide, which is now fully populated with the measured Optical Density (OD) values: 0.0, 0.06, 0.13, 0.19, 0.26, and 0.32, corresponding to each dilution. Red animated boxes highlight different columns of the table, including "Std Vol (mL)", "Drabkin's solution Vol (mL)", "Dilution factor", "OD", and "Value of Hb", as a voiceover explains the content of each column.

The video segment opens with a dark blue background displaying the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" and the subtitle "Preparation of Standard curve for Hemoglobin estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin method". A grid-lined graph, featuring a linear standard curve, is centered, with the horizontal axis labeled "Concentration of Hb (gm/L)" and the vertical axis marked with "Absorbance value", both highlighted by red arrows. The scene transitions to show two graphs side-by-side: one an Excel chart and the other a handwritten graph on paper, both depicting linear standard curves passing through the origin, which is circled in red on both. Text at the bottom clarifies, "Plotting on an Excel sheet will be discussed in next video". The graphs then disappear, replaced by text stating, "After OD of the sample is taken, the corresponding Hb value can be directly read, by plotting on the graph". The final shot is a close-up of a handwritten standard curve on graph paper titled "STANDARD CURVE FOR HB%", with details including "Drabkin's Solution Lot no: 12 B 4", "Concentration of Standard - 14.8 gm%", and signed "Dept. of Hematology, MGM Hospital, Warangal" with a date "27/1/2016". A gloved hand points to the graph as the narration explains that an OD of 0.32 (circled in red on the vertical axis) corresponds to approximately 10.5 (circled in red on the horizontal axis) hemoglobin concentration when plotted on the graph.

The video segment opens with a slide displaying the title "Hb Estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin Method" in gold text, followed by a subtitle "Preparation of Standard curve for Hemoglobin estimation by Cyanmethemoglobin method" in cyan text. Below this, a green arrow points to the text "A new calibration curve must be prepared whenever". Subsequently, a list of factors appears sequentially as blue bullet points: "Test method", "Colorimeter", and "Cuvette type". A vertical bracket then emerges next to these three points, with the gray text "Is Changed" positioned beside it. Finally, "Reagent lot" appears as a fourth blue bullet point, and the bracket extends to include it, indicating that a new calibration curve is needed if any of these four elements are changed.
